subject: Social Media
title: Age Verification Battles
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Age Verification Battles.

hook.text: You must be 13 to use Instagram. The check? A checkbox. A ten-year-old clicks 'yes' and enters.

buildup.text: COPPA, the U.S. children's privacy law, set 13 as the minimum age. Platforms comply on paper, not practice.

discovery.text: Australia banned social media for under-16s in 2024. The first country to set a meaningful age floor.

twist.text: Effective verification conflicts with privacy. Proving age means sharing identity documents—a different risk.

climax.text: Tech companies argue parents should supervise. Parents argue platforms should enforce. Nobody takes responsibility.

punchline.text: The gate is open. The guard is a checkbox.

quiz.question: What did Australia do about children and social media in 2024?
